guidance.overview: Qualification determines whether an opportunity is real, winnable, and worth pursuing. Use the MEDDIC framework as a checklist. Flag each dimension as Known, Partial, or Unknown at the end of each discovery interaction.

dimensions.name: Metrics
dimensions.key_question: What measurable outcome does the customer expect from solving this problem?

status_indicators.known: Customer has stated a specific operational or business target (e.g. recovery time under 4 hours, zero unplanned downtime).
status_indicators.partial: Customer has described a general improvement goal but no specific measure.

discovery_questions: How would you measure success at the end of this project?
What does 'high availability' mean for your team in concrete terms?

dimensions.name: Economic Buyer
dimensions.key_question: Who has final budget authority for this purchase?

status_indicators.partial: Role known but individual not identified.
status_indicators.unknown: No information on who approves spend.

discovery_questions: Who else would be involved in the final decision on something like this?
Is budget approval centralised or does each department control its own?

dimensions.name: Decision Criteria
dimensions.key_question: What factors will the customer use to choose a solution?

status_indicators.known: Customer has listed specific criteria (performance, support, integration, cost).
status_indicators.partial: One or two criteria mentioned but not a complete picture.

discovery_questions: When evaluating options, what factors matter most to your team?
Are there any must-have requirements a solution needs to meet?

dimensions.name: Decision Process
dimensions.key_question: What steps does the customer follow to make a purchase decision?

status_indicators.partial: Some steps known; timeline or approvers unclear.

discovery_questions: What does your internal approval process look like for a project of this size?
What would need to happen for you to move forward in the next quarter?

dimensions.name: Identify Pain
dimensions.key_question: Is the problem urgent, significant, and owned by someone with authority?

status_indicators.known: Specific pain confirmed with business impact stated.
status_indicators.partial: Pain mentioned but impact not quantified.
status_indicators.unknown: General interest only; no clear pain.

discovery_questions: What is the biggest risk if you do not address this in the next six months?
Is this a priority for your leadership team right now?

dimensions.name: Champion
dimensions.key_question: Is there an internal advocate who wants this to succeed and will represent us?

status_indicators.known: Individual identified; has engaged actively and shared internal context.
status_indicators.partial: Someone is interested but has not demonstrated internal influence.

discovery_questions: Who on your team would own the relationship with our technical team if we move forward?
Is there someone internally who would sponsor a proof of concept?

guidance_notes: A deal with more than two Unknown dimensions is high-risk. Prioritise uncovering Metrics and Economic Buyer first.
Do not push for all dimensions in one meeting. Qualification is an ongoing process.
Document the status after every customer interaction and share with the account team.
